title: Filesystem Edit Timestamp Capture Delivery
summary: let the local docs watcher advance last_updated for observed direct body, title, or summary edits without changing managed write or import ownership
content_html:
Filesystem Edit Timestamp Capture Delivery

Status And Purpose

Active as FET-1 under Roadmap.

FET-1 closes one local-authoring gap: when the running live watcher observes a direct filesystem edit to an existing canonical Markdown source, it advances last_updated if and only if the body, title, or summary changed.

This is independent of Docs Import. New, Import, the managed Source editor, and the metadata editor already own timestamps inside their mutation boundaries; FET-1 does not insert the watcher into those paths or add format-specific Import behavior.

Complete Outcome

While the local watcher is running, an author can edit an existing parent-scope or configured sub-scope Markdown file in VS Code and save it. After the normal debounce, the watcher:

  1. compares the previous and current parsed canonical source;
  2. recognises only body, title, or summary as recent-edit content;
  3. preserves a valid full last_updated already supplied by the author;
  4. otherwise rewrites only the timestamp fields with one full local timestamp;
  5. adopts its own source rewrite into the current watcher state; and
  6. performs the existing affected-collection rebuild once.

The source file remains canonical. Builders continue to project source without mutating it, and the watcher does not enter a self-triggered rewrite/rebuild loop.

Timestamp Contract

  • The positive allowlist is the shared recent_edit_content comparison: body, title, and summary, with no second definition in the watcher.
  • A change only to parent_id, viewable, ui_status, group, ordering, added_date, last_updated, filename, or other front matter does not qualify.
  • The watcher acts only when one current document can be matched to one previous document with the same immutable doc_id. Rename-only changes do not advance the timestamp.
  • If qualifying content changed and the current last_updated is a valid full timestamp different from the previous value, it is explicit author evidence and is preserved.
  • Otherwise the watcher supplies a full YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM:SS local timestamp. It must be strictly later than the previous full timestamp; a same-second save uses the earliest representable later second without sleeping.
  • One debounce batch captures one timestamp for all qualifying files so their write evidence is internally consistent.
  • Existing added_date is preserved. If it is missing, the existing shared timestamp rewrite helper may restore it according to the current source-model rule; FET-1 adds no provenance inference.

New files are not silently repaired by this feature. Their creator or importer owns initial identity and date metadata, and invalid or ambiguous source continues through existing validation and error reporting rather than a best-effort mutation.

Watcher And Rebuild Contract

  • The mutation occurs after a successful parsed comparison and before the existing docs/search rebuild for the affected collection.
  • Parent scopes retain targeted affected-ID calculation and fallback behavior. Configured sub-scopes gain the same parsed previous/current comparison while retaining their confined rebuild owner.
  • Timestamp rewriting is atomic and preserves unrelated raw front-matter spelling, quoting, ordering, comments, and body bytes.
  • The watcher updates its file and parsed snapshots after its own rewrite so the next poll does not treat that rewrite as new author work.
  • One author save batch produces at most one timestamp rewrite per qualifying document and one normal rebuild pass for the collection.
  • If timestamp writing fails, the watcher reports the failure and does not present the timestamp as captured. The existing source remains available for correction and a later save/retry.
  • If the source rewrite succeeds but the projection rebuild fails, the timestamp remains canonical source evidence. Existing rebuild retry behavior handles projection recovery without rewriting the timestamp again.
  • Docs-management suppression markers remain the owner for New, Import, Source, and metadata writes. A fully suppressed managed batch is adopted without FET-1 comparison or mutation.

Boundary

In scope:

  • direct edits observed while the local watcher is running;
  • existing top-level and configured sub-scope Markdown documents;
  • the shared body/title/summary positive allowlist;
  • valid manual timestamp preservation;
  • atomic timestamp-only source rewriting;
  • deterministic same-second advancement;
  • self-write adoption and no-loop behavior; and
  • focused source-model, watcher, parent-scope, and sub-scope evidence.

Not in scope:

  • changes to ordinary, package, returned-package, or edited-review Import;
  • changes to New, managed Source, or metadata-editor timestamp ownership;
  • builder-side source mutation;
  • edits made while the watcher is stopped, startup backfill, Git-history inference, or filesystem-mtime inference;
  • automatic repair of new, malformed, duplicate, or identity-changing source;
  • widening Recently Edited beyond body, title, and summary;
  • timezone, timestamp format, or date-provenance migration; or
  • production/public runtime behavior.

Likely Authority

  • docs_source_model.py retains the shared recent-edit comparison, timestamp validation, advancement, and raw-front-matter rewrite helpers.
  • docs_live_rebuild_watcher.py owns observed previous/current snapshots, exact-document matching, batch timestamp choice, self-write adoption, and rebuild sequencing.
  • docs_write_rebuild.py retains management-write suppression and collection rebuild ownership.
  • Existing create, import, Source, and metadata services remain the exclusive timestamp owners for their managed mutations.
  • The docs and search builders remain read-only consumers of canonical source.

Delivery Tracker

[x] FET-1.0 — Freeze Comparison And Rewrite Semantics

  • [x] Turn the existing warning comparison into a reusable plan that reports exact matched documents, qualifying content changes, manual timestamp evidence, and required rewrites without writing.
  • [x] Freeze stable-identity, same-second, batch-timestamp, invalid-source, and write-failure behavior in focused source-model and watcher tests.

Evidence:

  • direct_edit_timestamp_plan is a pure previous/current snapshot plan. Same-path and renamed files match only through one stable doc_id; new, identity-changing, ambiguous, missing-snapshot, or invalid comparison input remains non-mutating.
  • Body, title, and summary use the shared recent_edit_content tuple. A valid different full timestamp is preserved as manual evidence; an invalid or unchanged value requires rewrite.
  • Every required rewrite in one plan receives one replacement timestamp after the latest comparable previous value. The source-model helper resolves same-second and backwards-clock candidates without sleeping.
  • The two focused Python files pass 30 tests. Explicit four-file Python lint and bytecode compilation pass. The atomic-write failure specimen preserves the original destination and removes its temporary file.

Stop and review the comparison plan and evidence before FET-1.1.

[ ] FET-1.1 — Capture Parent-Scope Filesystem Edits

  • [ ] Apply atomic timestamp rewrites before the existing parent-scope rebuild and adopt the rewritten file and parsed snapshots.
  • [ ] Prove body, title, and summary saves advance once; manual valid timestamps, non-qualifying metadata, rename-only changes, New, Source, metadata, and Import writes remain untouched.

Stop and review parent-scope source diffs, logs, rebuild count, and focused evidence before FET-1.2.

[ ] FET-1.2 — Add Configured Sub-Scope Parity

  • [ ] Generalise parsed snapshots to an exact configured document collection without falling back from a sub-scope to its parent scope.
  • [ ] Prove the same capture, preservation, self-write, failure, and no-loop behavior in Analysis/Tags or an equivalent configured sub-scope.

Stop and review collection confinement and parent-versus-sub-scope parity before FET-1.3.

[ ] FET-1.3 — Realistic Acceptance And Authority Transfer

  • [ ] Run the focused Python suite, maintained watcher/suppression checks, and realistic local watcher acceptance for qualifying and non-qualifying direct saves in both collection kinds.
  • [ ] Update Live Rebuild Watcher and Document Identity from shipped behavior, then rebuild Studio docs and search.
  • [ ] Independently inspect the final source/generated diff and record exact evidence and omissions here before marking FET-1 complete.

Completion Gate

FET-1 is complete only when a realistic running-watcher exercise proves all of the following for both a top-level scope and a configured sub-scope:

  • direct body, title, and summary saves advance last_updated exactly once and publish the edited result in one collection rebuild;
  • a supplied valid full timestamp is preserved;
  • non-qualifying metadata and rename-only saves do not advance;
  • same-second qualifying saves receive deterministic later timestamps;
  • managed New, Import, Source, and metadata writes remain single-owner and do not receive a second watcher timestamp;
  • watcher-authored timestamp rewrites do not schedule another mutation or rebuild pass; and
  • builders remain projection-only.

Current state: FET-1.0 is complete. The watcher still reports timestamp evidence warnings and performs no timestamp mutation. Stop before FET-1.1.
